approvedThesis.intent: Create the digital launch experience for a contemporary design museum exhibition about patina, repair, wear and material memory. The experience must make physical time perceptible without turning the site into a cinematic demo or sacrificing reading, wayfinding, ticketing and accessibility.
approvedThesis.audience: Design-literate museum visitors, architects, product designers, students and culturally curious general visitors using desktop and mobile devices.
approvedThesis.commercialObjective: Make the exhibition memorable while preserving clear access to dates, location, events and ticket reservation.

governingIdea.statement: Let accumulated material change become the exhibition’s evidence system, so time is perceived through what the objects have endured rather than through decorative spectacle.

approvedThesis.statement: Let accumulated material change become the exhibition’s evidence system, so time is perceived through what the objects have endured rather than through decorative spectacle. Creative tension: archival authority x tactile sensuality. Truth anchor: The exhibition contains one hundred real objects whose scratches, repairs, fading and deformation are evidence of use rather than defects to hide.
approvedThesis.whyThisProject: After Matter is about one hundred real objects whose wear, repair, fading and deformation are evidence of use. The thesis keeps those histories primary while preserving reading, wayfinding, ticketing, mobile access and reduced-motion meaning.

sourceTruths.value: The exhibition contains one hundred real objects whose scratches, repairs, fading and deformation are evidence of use rather than defects to hide.
Visitors need both contemplative editorial reading and practical access to dates, location, events and ticket reservation.
The museum wants a memorable digital identity for the exhibition but rejects spectacle that overwhelms the objects themselves.
Mobile is a primary visit-planning surface, not a reduced desktop afterthought.
Reduced-motion users must receive equivalent hierarchy, causality and narrative meaning rather than a stripped fallback.
Motion must derive from accumulated time, material memory, repair or change; technology cannot become the concept.
Long-form reading requires deliberate stillness and stable hierarchy.
Primary navigation, exhibition information and ticket reservation remain immediately usable throughout the experience.
Desktop and mobile require authored reinterpretation rather than scaled copies.
Reduced-motion behavior preserves semantic sequence and state meaning.
The experience remains plausible for production performance and accessibility budgets.
Real objects remain primary visual evidence; generic synthetic hero imagery cannot replace them.

categoryRejections: Generic scroll-triggered fade-and-rise sequences applied uniformly to every section.
Floating glass cards, glowing AI gradients or decorative particles unrelated to material memory.
Continuous camera drift or parallax used only to signal premium aesthetics.
Over-elastic spring motion that makes museum content feel playful or weightless without conceptual reason.
Scroll-jacking that delays reading or practical tasks.
Reduced motion implemented by simply disabling everything and losing narrative relationships.
principles: Accumulated material change must remain connected to real object histories rather than decorative atmosphere.
Stillness is the default state for reading, comparison and practical museum tasks.
Repair and accumulated change are evidence of use, not luxury surface treatment.
Each medium interprets the evidence system differently without replacing real objects with synthetic spectacle.
antiPrinciples: Generic scroll-triggered fade-and-rise sequences applied uniformly to every section.
Floating glass cards, glowing AI gradients or decorative particles unrelated to material memory.
Continuous camera drift or parallax used only to signal premium aesthetics.

Scroll-jacking that delays reading or practical tasks.
Reduced motion implemented by simply disabling everything and losing narrative relationships.

expressionTests.typography: Separate contemplative exhibition voice from factual trace labels and durable reading without making type compete with object evidence.
expressionTests.image: Use licensed object photography or new capture to show actual wear, repair and material change; Phase 0 placeholders remain explicitly non-documentary.
expressionTests.motion: Make changes in material condition or historical understanding perceptible when they matter, then preserve deliberate stillness; no continuous drift.
expressionTests.interaction: Let visitors encounter objects and their material histories without losing orientation or access to practical museum routes.
expressionTests.sound: Silence remains the default; any later sound must be grounded in object evidence and retain a silent equivalent.
expressionTests.responsive: On desktop, mobile and under reduced motion, preserve the same evidence relationships, reading clarity and access to practical museum tasks through authored reinterpretation.

approvedThesis.technologyPolicy: Implementation tools serve the evidence system. Motion, browser APIs, generated media and spatial tools are considered only when they make object-specific material time more legible without displacing the objects or museum tasks.

competitorTransferTest.question: Could another museum or design site reuse this evidence-system Thesis unchanged without the specific collection truth that wear, repair, fading and deformation are meaningful records of use?
competitorTransferTest.passCondition: The Thesis should weaken without After Matter’s one hundred real objects and its requirement to make accumulated material time perceptible while preserving reading, wayfinding, ticketing, mobile access and reduced-motion equivalence.

alternativesConsidered.idea: Treat repair, care, uncertainty and alteration as the exhibition's public record, making preservation itself a readable editorial structure rather than a hidden conservation backstory.
alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Most intellectually distinct, but risks making one hundred object encounters feel like an archive interface rather than an exhibition experience.

alternativesConsidered.idea: Make one hundred distinct object lives perceptible as a shared tempo: each encounter isolates a particular change, while deliberate stillness lets the collection cohere without flattening its differences.
alternativesConsidered.rejectedBecause: Best collection-scale frame, but less immediately actionable for wayfinding and may dilute the specificity of repair as evidence.

approvedThesis.selectionRationale: This recovery Thesis is the broadest project-specific governing idea supported by the frozen After Matter brief: material change is meaningful evidence, but the later Creative World determines whether that evidence becomes navigation, editorial record, collection rhythm, or another materially grounded behavior.
unresolvedRisks: Final licensed object photography and object-specific historical records remain outside this recovery pass.

authoringBrief.instruction: Author 3–5 genuinely different experience worlds that all preserve the same thesis but differ in narrative, composition, image/material behavior, motion, interaction, and responsive logic. Do not submit palette/type/layout reskins.

worlds.label: Friction Index
worlds.worldIdea: Accumulated marks of use become the visitor's wayfinding system, so the exhibition is entered through a trace rather than a spectacle.
worlds.interpretationOfThesis: Material time becomes a readable sequence of specific changes: wear, repair, fading, and care guide attention while objects, reading, and practical museum tasks remain primary.
worlds.signatureBehavior: A visitor chooses one material trace at a time; the chosen trace reveals its history, then the interface holds still long enough for inspection and reading.
worlds.narrativeModel: move from a visible object to one selected trace, then from that trace into history, context, and a return to the object.
worlds.compositionModel: a high-contrast object field paired with an ordered trace index and calm reading column; practical routes remain visible at every state.

typographyIntent.statement: Typography separates an expansive contemplative exhibition voice from compact, factual trace labels and stable long-form reading; no final family or weight is approved.
antiPatterns: monumental type that competes with objects

worlds.imageLanguage: licensed exhibition object photography or new museum capture presented with close material crops, visible wear, and enough negative space for one factual trace at a time; Phase 0 uses an explicitly non-documentary material placeholder only.
worlds.materialLanguage: oxidized metal, repaired ceramic, worn lacquer, paper fiber, dark archival cloth, fine rules, and restrained oxide-red trace markers.
worlds.motionLanguage: single-trace reveals, deliberate pauses, and quiet contextual returns; no continuous camera drift, uniform fades, or decorative particles.
worlds.interactionModel: choose a material trace, inspect its history, move between object detail and exhibition context without losing orientation, and access visit information immediately.
worlds.responsiveStrategy: mobile retains one trace at a time with the current object and return route visible; reading and ticket routes recompose vertically rather than inheriting desktop columns.
worlds.soundPolicy: Silence by default. Any future sound must be tied to real object evidence, have rights clearance, and preserve a silent equivalent.

worlds.label: Repair Ledger
worlds.worldIdea: Care is the editorial voice: repair, uncertainty and conservation records gather beside each object as a public, readable ledger.

worlds.signatureBehavior: Annotations gather beside the object, then settle into a stable chronological ledger that remains readable without pulling attention away from the object.
worlds.narrativeModel: move from object encounter into a chronological ledger of care, uncertainty and context, then return to the object with the record retained.
worlds.compositionModel: object field with a calm adjacent ledger, durable reading column and compact visit rail; documentation is ordered as evidence rather than ornament.

typographyIntent.statement: A measured editorial hierarchy distinguishes object title, conservation annotation, uncertainty and long-form curatorial reading without approving a final family.
antiPatterns: type that makes care feel bureaucratic

worlds.materialLanguage: paper fiber, conservation tissue, graphite notation, repaired joins, archival tabs and restrained ink rules.
worlds.motionLanguage: annotations gather and settle into chronology, followed by still reading; no theatrical reveal or ambient drift.
worlds.interactionModel: inspect a care record, compare sequential interventions, retain object context and reach visit tasks immediately.

worlds.label: Pressure Room
worlds.worldIdea: Time is felt as resistance: one object receives a concentrated encounter where pressure and release make quiet attention the dramatic event.
worlds.interpretationOfThesis: Accumulated change is understood through a focused encounter with the resistance an object has endured, then released into factual history and practical museum access.
worlds.signatureBehavior: A deliberate threshold concentrates attention on one object-history relationship, then releases into stable context without forcing waiting or blocking access.
worlds.narrativeModel: arrive at one object, experience a composed threshold of resistance, open its factual history, then release back to a still exhibition field.
worlds.compositionModel: one dominant object plane, a compressed threshold edge and a surrounding still field with persistent practical navigation.

typographyIntent.statement: Sparse spatial typography holds attention around one object while factual history and practical routes stay immediately legible; no final family is approved.
avoidCategories: oversized type that blocks the object

worlds.imageLanguage: licensed object photography or new capture shown at concentrated scale with materially specific close detail; this proof uses an explicitly labelled non-documentary material-study placeholder.
worlds.materialLanguage: dark mineral ground, compressed shadow, worn surfaces, fine pressure lines and restrained light at repaired edges.
worlds.motionLanguage: brief resistance, release and long stillness; reduced motion preserves the same threshold relationship as a stable state change.
worlds.interactionModel: enter or bypass a composed object threshold, inspect its factual history, return to the exhibition field and access visit tasks at every point.
worlds.responsiveStrategy: mobile uses a vertical encounter sequence with a visible bypass and immediate visit route; pressure is expressed through hierarchy, never elapsed time.
worlds.soundPolicy: Silence by default. Any future sound must support an object-specific causal relationship and retain a silent equivalent.

categoryTransferTest.whyProjectSpecific: The encounter is specific to After Matter because one hundred real objects carry distinct resistance through wear, repair, fading and deformation, not because a generic cultural site needs theatrical tension.
categoryTransferTest.transferRisk: high if the threshold turns into a cinematic intro, scroll-jacking or a technology demonstration.

unresolvedRisks: The threshold requires clear bypass and reduced-motion equivalence.

worlds.label: Pressure Room
worlds.worldIdea: Time is felt as resistance: one object receives a concentrated encounter where pressure and release make quiet attention the dramatic event.
worlds.interpretationOfThesis: Accumulated change is understood through a focused encounter with the resistance an object has endured, then released into factual history and practical museum access.
worlds.signatureBehavior: A deliberate threshold concentrates attention on one object-history relationship, then releases into stable context without forcing waiting or blocking access.
worlds.narrativeModel: arrive at one object, experience a composed threshold of resistance, open its factual history, then release back to a still exhibition field.
worlds.compositionModel: one dominant object plane, a compressed threshold edge and a surrounding still field with persistent practical navigation.

typographyIntent.statement: Sparse spatial typography holds attention around one object while factual history and practical routes stay immediately legible; no final family is approved.
avoidCategories: oversized type that blocks the object

worlds.imageLanguage: licensed object photography or new capture shown at concentrated scale with materially specific close detail; this proof uses an explicitly labelled non-documentary material-study placeholder.
worlds.materialLanguage: dark mineral ground, compressed shadow, worn surfaces, fine pressure lines and restrained light at repaired edges.
worlds.motionLanguage: brief resistance, release and long stillness; reduced motion preserves the same threshold relationship as a stable state change.
worlds.interactionModel: enter or bypass a composed object threshold, inspect its factual history, return to the exhibition field and access visit tasks at every point.
worlds.responsiveStrategy: mobile uses a vertical encounter sequence with a visible bypass and immediate visit route; pressure is expressed through hierarchy, never elapsed time.
worlds.soundPolicy: Silence by default. Any future sound must support an object-specific causal relationship and retain a silent equivalent.

categoryTransferTest.whyProjectSpecific: The encounter is specific to After Matter because one hundred real objects carry distinct resistance through wear, repair, fading and deformation, not because a generic cultural site needs theatrical tension.
categoryTransferTest.transferRisk: high if the threshold turns into a cinematic intro, scroll-jacking or a technology demonstration.

thesisRef.governingIdea: Let accumulated material change become the exhibition’s evidence system, so time is perceived through what the objects have endured rather than through decorative spectacle.

unresolvedRisks: The threshold requires clear bypass and reduced-motion equivalence.
Concentration must not suppress reading, dates, location or ticket access.
